title: Best Blenders UK
short: Portable, personal and full-size blenders compared by power, jug capacity and who they suit.
intro: Blenders range from pocket-sized portable bottles to powerful full-size machines that grind nuts and crush ice. This guide compares blenders from Expert Reviews' testing, from budget personal blenders to premium countertop models, so you can match the power and capacity to what you actually blend.

products.name: A2300i Ascent Series
products.best_for: Buyers who want maximum power and versatility
products.summary: Expert Reviews' premium pick. It crushes ice effortlessly, makes nut butters and grinds coffee beans, with app connectivity and a 10-year warranty, at a high price.
pros: Makes nut butters and grinds beans

products.name: K150
products.best_for: Buyers who want strong build quality for everyday blending
products.summary: A well-built blender that crushed half an ice tray in 10 seconds in testing, with a classic design and a useful pulse function, though it is pricey for a fairly basic feature set.
pros: Crushes half an ice tray in 10 seconds

products.name: NutriPro 1000
products.best_for: Buyers who want strong performance without premium pricing
products.summary: A well-built blender with a heavy, stable base and two lidded cups included, offering excellent value, though it is notably loud and struggles slightly with tough greens.
pros: Well-built with a heavy, stable base
cons: Struggles slightly with tough greens like kale

products.name: 600 Series
products.summary: A personal blender that produces silky-smooth results and processes fibrous vegetables quickly, with small and large cups included, though its ice-crushing is limited.
pros: Processes fibrous vegetables in under 30 seconds

products.name: Blend Active Personal
products.best_for: Buyers who want an affordable personal blender
products.summary: Expert Reviews' budget pick. It crushes ice and comes with two portable jugs with leak-proof lids, though its motor is less powerful than pricier rivals.
pros: Two portable jugs with leak-proof lids

products.best_for: Gym bags, travel and blending on the go
products.summary: A compact, cordless, rechargeable blender that gives around 15 blends per charge, though it has only one speed and a small jug.

products.name: Daily Collection Mini
products.best_for: Small kitchens that still want to grind nuts and coffee
products.summary: A compact blender that is powerful for its size and comes with a glass jug and an on-the-go tumbler, though its working capacity is limited for family-sized servings.

guide.a: Personal blenders like the Nutribullet or BlendJet suit single smoothies you drink straight from the cup. Full-size blenders with a larger jug suit families, soups, and batch-making, and generally offer more power for ice and tough ingredients.

guide.q: How much power do I actually need?
guide.a: For smoothies with soft fruit, 300-600W is usually enough. For crushing ice regularly, or grinding nuts, coffee beans or hard vegetables, look for 1,000W or more.

guide.q: Do I need multiple speed settings?
guide.a: Multiple speeds and a pulse function give more control, useful for chopping rather than fully blending, or for building up to a smooth texture with tough ingredients. A single-speed blender is simpler but less flexible.

guide.q: Is a portable blender worth it?
guide.a: A USB-rechargeable portable blender like the BlendJet is useful for the gym, travel or a desk, but has a small capacity and less power than a plugged-in blender, so it is best as a second blender rather than your only one.
